parts.latex: Hence, or otherwise, find the values of $x$ for which $y=\ln(\cot x)$ is defined in the interval $0\le x\le 2\pi$.

solutions.latex:
$\cot x=\dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x}$.

Vertical asymptotes where $\sin x=0$: $x=0,\ \pi,\ 2\pi$.

$x$-intercepts where $\cos x=0$: $x=\dfrac{\pi}{2},\ \dfrac{3\pi}{2}$.

$\cot x$ is decreasing on each branch, since $\dfrac{d}{dx}\cot x=-\operatorname{cosec}^2x<0$.

parts.latex:
Prove that

$$\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{1+\sin x}{\cos x}\right)=\dfrac{1+\sin x}{\cos^2 x}$$

Hence, or otherwise, show that

$$\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\ln(\sec x+\tan x)\right]=\sec x$$

solutions.latex:
Using the quotient rule, $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{u}{v}\right)=\dfrac{u'v-uv'}{v^2}$, with
$$\begin{aligned} u&=1+\sin x & v&=\cos x\\ u'&=\cos x & v'&=-\sin x\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{1+\sin x}{\cos x}\right)&=\dfrac{\cos x(\cos x)-(-\sin x)(1+\sin x)}{\cos^2 x}\\ &=\dfrac{\cos^2 x+\sin x+\sin^2 x}{\cos^2 x}\\ &=\dfrac{1+\sin x}{\cos^2 x}\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Makes one mistake, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
$$\sec x+\tan x=\dfrac{1}{\cos x}+\dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}=\dfrac{1+\sin x}{\cos x}$$
From part (a):
$$\begin{aligned} f(x)&=\dfrac{1+\sin x}{\cos x} \\ f'(x)&=\dfrac{1+\sin x}{\cos^2 x} \end{aligned}$$
Using $\dfrac{d}{dx}\ln f(x)=\dfrac{f'(x)}{f(x)}$:
$$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{d}{dx}\ln(\sec x+\tan x)&=\dfrac{d}{dx}\ln\left(\dfrac{1+\sin x}{\cos x}\right)\\ &=\dfrac{1+\sin x}{\cos^2 x}\times\dfrac{\cos x}{1+\sin x}\\ &=\dfrac{1}{\cos x}=\sec x\end{aligned}$$
Hence proved.
criteria: Simplifies the expression, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: If $f(x)=\ln(\cos x)$, find the value of $f'\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$.

solutions.latex:

$$\begin{aligned}f'(x)&=\dfrac{-\sin x}{\cos x}\\&=-\tan x\end{aligned}$$
When $x=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$:
$$\begin{aligned}f'\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)&=-\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\\&=-1\end{aligned}$$

Using the log laws first:
$$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{d}{dx}\Big[\ln\left(e^x\sin x\right)\Big]&=\dfrac{d}{dx}\Big[\ln e^x+\ln(\sin x)\Big]\\&=\dfrac{d}{dx}\Big[x+\ln(\sin x)\Big]\\&=1+\cot x\end{aligned}$$
Alternative, using the product rule, $\dfrac{d}{dx}(uv)=u'v+uv'$, with
$$\begin{aligned}u&=e^x & v&=\sin x\\u'&=e^x & v'&=\cos x\end{aligned}$$
$$\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(e^x\sin x\right)=e^x\cos x+e^x\sin x$$
Then, using $\dfrac{d}{dx}\ln f(x)=\dfrac{f'(x)}{f(x)}$:
$$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{d}{dx}\Big[\ln\left(e^x\sin x\right)\Big]&=\dfrac{e^x(\cos x+\sin x)}{e^x\sin x}\\&=\dfrac{\cos x+\sin x}{\sin x}\\&=1+\cot x\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Attempts to use the product rule correctly, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: Find the derivative of $y=\ln\sqrt{\dfrac{x+1}{x-1}}$, giving your answer in simplest form.

solutions.latex:
Using log laws to expand before differentiating:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=\ln\left(\dfrac{x+1}{x-1}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\&=\dfrac{1}{2}\Big[\ln(x+1)-\ln(x-1)\Big]\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{dy}{dx}&=\dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{1}{x+1}-\dfrac{1}{x-1}\right]\\&=\dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{x-1-(x+1)}{x^2-1}\right]\\&=\dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{-2}{x^2-1}\right]\\&=\dfrac{-1}{x^2-1}\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Uses log laws to expand, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: Hence, when $x=2$, Show that $f'(x)=\dfrac{2\sqrt{x}+1}{2x\left(\sqrt{x}+1\right)}$ can be written in the form $a+b\sqrt{2}$

solutions.latex:
Using the chain rule on $f(x)=\log_e\left(x+\sqrt{x}\right)$:

$$\begin{aligned} f'(x) &= \dfrac{1}{x+\sqrt{x}}\left[1+\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\right] \\ &= \dfrac{1}{x+\sqrt{x}}\times\dfrac{2\sqrt{x}+1}{2\sqrt{x}} \\ &= \dfrac{2\sqrt{x}+1}{\left(x+\sqrt{x}\right)\times 2\sqrt{x}} \\ &= \dfrac{2\sqrt{x}+1}{\sqrt{x}\left(\sqrt{x}+1\right)\times 2\sqrt{x}} \\ &= \dfrac{2\sqrt{x}+1}{2x\left(\sqrt{x}+1\right)} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Writes the chain rule form, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:

$$\begin{aligned} f'(2) &= \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}+1}{2\times 2\left(\sqrt{2}+1\right)} \\ &= \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}+1}{4\left(\sqrt{2}+1\right)}\times\dfrac{\sqrt{2}-1}{\sqrt{2}-1} \\ &= \dfrac{4-2\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{2}-1}{4(2-1)} \\ &= \dfrac{3-\sqrt{2}}{4} \\ &= \dfrac{3}{4}-\dfrac{1}{4}\sqrt{2} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Substitutes and rationalises, or equivalent merit
